messages.subject: Inconsistent D = 1.702?
parts:
Dear Phil,

I have two related questions. First, it appears that the scaling constant D is no longer automatically set to 1.702 and that the value cannot be changed. For example, if I simulate data and compare the results as in:

N <- 10000
J <- 20
d <- rnorm(J)
a <- exp(rmvnorm(J,c(0),diag(.25,1)))
theta <- rmvnorm(N,c(0),diag(1,1))
x <- array(NA,c(N,J))
for(i in 1:N){for(j in 1:J){x[i,j] <- as.numeric(1/(1+exp(-1.0*(d[j]+theta[i]*a[j]))) > runif(1))}}
mr1 <- mirt(x,model = 1)
cbind(round(a,3),unlist(coef(mr1))[seq(1,4*J,4)])

I find that (1) the mirt a parameter estimates are consistent with D = 1.0 in the simulation, (2) changing D to 1.7 in the simulation (not shown) results in parameters that do not match, and (3) trying to change D within the mirt function (i.e., adding D = 1.702 or D = 1.0 as a function parameter) has no effect. Can you confirm that D is now fixed to 1.0 in all models and cannot be changed (sorry if I missed this in the manual)?

Second, I'm fitting a multidimensional model with fixed a parameters and fixed d parameters (with thetas completely unconstrained). The reasons are substitutive. The parameter estimates in this model are consistent with D = 1.702. That is, if I save the a parameters, d parameters, and theta parameters to environment variables and then try to predict the observed data using a logistic function, the results are accurate when D = 1.702 but inaccurate when D = 1.0. Interestingly, I'm fitting other models were the a parameters but not the d parameters are constrained, and in those instances the results are accurate when D = 1.0. I realize this is very idiosyncratic, and I cannot promise that I'm not making some type of error, but can you think of any reason why the program might change the value of D depending on the types of constraints placed on the parameters (and is there anyway to verify what value of D was used)?

I'm using mirt Version 1.13.

Thank you,

Michael

Yes, the D scaling coef should appear nowhere in the package and therefore D=1 is implied. I found including it change the numerical convergence criteria too much, therefore it was removed some time ago.

That is, if I save the a parameters, d parameters, and theta parameters to environment variables and then try to predict the observed data using a logistic function, the results are accurate when D = 1.702 but inaccurate when D = 1.0. Interestingly, I'm fitting other models were the a parameters but not the d parameters are constrained, and in those instances the results are accurate when D = 1.0. I realize this is very idiosyncratic, and I cannot promise that I'm not making some type of error, but can you think of any reason why the program might change the value of D depending on the types of constraints placed on the parameters (and is there anyway to verify what value of D was used)?

I think the best way to just to check the change log to see when the constant was removed. The current dev version is located here: https://github.com/philchalmers/mirt/blob/master/NEWS.md. It sounds very much like older versions were being compared, which I don't always guarantee are reverse compatible. Though without seeing some code, it's really difficult for me to say. HTH.

Phil

I'm using mirt Version 1.13.

Thank you,

Michael
